rationale: Beat EPS ($2.59 vs $2.45), 9 consecutive quarters of gross margin expansion to record 37.9%, revenue +30% YoY, FY25 revenue +39%. Nearline exabyte capacity sold out through mid-2026 via build-to-order contracts with visibility building into 2H. Three major CSPs qualified on HAMR/Mozaic 3, 4TB/disk qualification started with global CSP, volume ramp early 2026. Management resuming share repurchases, confident and direct in Q&A pushing back on analysts' conservative models. Guide $2.5B Q1 ±$150M implies continued margin expansion; CFO said gross margin up 'much higher than 50bps sequentially.' Demand described as 'above supply.' Multiple forward catalysts (HAMR ramp, 4TB/disk ramp, exabyte crossover 2H26). Tone extremely confident.

Strong beat with aggressive Q4 guide $920M-$1B (huge seq jump from $769M Q3), driven by AI compute/HBM/networking with project pull-ins. Q3 memory revenue doubled QoQ to $128M, SoC +11% sequential. Management says 2026 'looks stronger today than 6 months ago.' New merchant GPU customer wins excluded from guide (potential upside). Counterbalances: CFO Sanjay Mehta stepping down (though new CFO named and well-credentialed), robotics still weak at $75M flat QoQ, management explicitly warned against 'drawing a line straight up' from Q3-Q4 — Q4 is 'new high watermark,' with pull-ins from Q1/Q2 into Q4 creating air-pocket risk early 2026. One-time gross margin pressure from expedited supply costs. Mobile SoC 'we don't know' magnitude of 2026 recovery. Net positive but guarded.

Coach accelerating into Q1 with strong brand heat (Kisslock bag sold out in hours, 1M new NA customers, 70% Gen Z/millennial), Q1 revenue guide 'low double digits' vs Q4's 13%, Q1 EPS guide +20% to ~$1.25. Record 76.3% Q4 gross margin, +210bps FY. FY25 EPS $5.10, returned $2.3B to shareholders. Dividend raised 14%. Offsets: $850M non-cash Kate Spade impairment, $160M tariff headwind (230bps margin pressure) only 30% mitigated in guide, Kate Spade revenue -13% in Q4 and guided down high single digits for FY26, full-year EPS growth only 4-7%. Japan -11%. Coach story strong and gaining, but FY guidance is heavy in first half, tariff overhang is real, and the impairment + Kate Spade drag creates mixed optics.

Clean EPS beat ($3.66 vs $3.05), $1.6B refining segment profit (3x prior year), 97% utilization with Gulf Coast and North Atlantic records. Ethanol record production ($183M). Returned $1.3B to shareholders in Q3 (78% payout ratio), $2.6B YTD. Bullish macro setup in Q&A: low inventories, widening sour differentials (WCS discount to Brent widened from 7% to 12%, Maya 14%), 460k bpd demand growth vs 415k capacity additions in 2026 with capacity unlikely to hit nameplate, Russian sanctions potentially bullish for product cracks. Strong export demand, tight supply persisting. Offsets: Renewable Diesel lost $28M, Benicia closure $0.25/share quarterly drag for 2 more quarters, DGD still losing money though turning. Macro tailwinds + aggressive buybacks are key. Bullish overall.

Modest beat ($0.67 vs $0.63), but only 1% operational revenue growth, total revenues DOWN 1% YoY. North America -12%, Japan -9%. Indore FDA facility issues unresolved — reinspection timing out of company's control, 'likely unannounced in 2026.' Company is building redundancies to decouple from Indore but acknowledges uncertainty. Pipeline-dependent story with catalysts mostly 2026+ (meloxicam NDA by year-end, estrogen patch mid-2026 approval, cenerimod Phase III readout 'around year-end 2026', selatogrel even later). Government shutdown risk to NDA submissions. No 2026 guidance provided. 'Enterprise-wide strategic review' cost cutting announced but quantum deferred to Q1 2026 investor event — typically a red flag of deteriorating business (if things were great, wouldn't need a review). Amitiza LOE in Japan noted as 2026 headwind. Management tone uses hedging language ('durable' 'balanced' 'exploring') and repeatedly defers concrete numbers. Growth is pipeline-promise rather than current execution. More red flags than positives for next 30 days.
